verified.title: Unclean Host exit drops provider processes from the promotion gate
verified.boundary: Promotion of paired-device staged changes (promoteStaged live-code gate) after a Host crash or kill. Not a HIGH for this boundary: the phone gains no execution authority, the owner performs the promotion, and the surviving process is already workstation-authorized shell code.
verified.reproduction: 1) Start a Codex write Mission (shell-capable authority) so a provider process is spawned. 2) Stage a paired-device change into the Mission project. 3) Kill the Host process without a clean shutdown (for example taskkill /F on the Host). 4) Restart the Host. On restart the task is marked failed and the process is left running. 5) Approve promotion of the staged change. liveCodeExecutions() sees no sessions, no lingering survivors and no bus liveCode entries, so promotion proceeds while the surviving provider process can still read or run the project. Not runtime-verified; derived from code reading and Windows child-process semantics (children are not killed when the parent dies).
verified.evidence: src/lib/bunny-host/adapters.server.ts:208 (provider child is plain spawnChild; trackOwnedChild only adds it to an in-memory Set for graceful stop), :326 (Codex Mission path also uses spawnSession). src/lib/bunny-host/owned-processes.server.ts:11-19, :34-50 (in-memory owned set; graceful stop only). src/lib/bunny-host/manager.server.ts:77-84 (lingering and lingeringAttempt are in-memory maps), :156-166 (restart marks running tasks failed with 'no process was killed'; no watchSurvivors reseed; watchSurvivors call sites are only :1431 and :1654). src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:2646-2647 (promotion gate calls liveCodeExecutions), :2725-2741 (sessions, lingering and bus.liveCode, all in-memory). Persisted data that could seed the gate is available: task.pid and processTree are written at manager.server.ts:1226-1240 and :1677. The native KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE job (native/bunny-owned-process.c:85) covers only Git, gh and terminal.exec, so a crash does not reap provider processes.
verified.repair: Pure Node, using existing helpers (process-tree.server.ts sameProcessIdentity, survivors, descendants). (a) Persist the root process creation time at the session hook (manager.server.ts:1226-1240) so the root can be identity-checked. (b) At Host startup, for each task that was launching/running/verifying/waiting, sample processTable once and seed lingering with the persisted processTree rows (and the root) that match by pid, createdAt and name, using the task's provider/access. (c) If a persisted root pid cannot be identity-verified, hold promotion (refuse with a 'code from before the restart may still run' reason) until the owner confirms in the UI or a later sample shows the pid gone. Add a test that restarts the manager with a seeded survivor and asserts promotion is refused.

1. Documented residual. MA3_T9R_F01_SECURITY_CLOSURE.md:201 states "Survivor tracking is in memory. Processes surviving a Host restart are not tracked; remote envelopes are revoked at restart." It is not a new containment defect.

2. The repro's step order is impossible. Step 2 stages a change before the crash, and step 5 approves its promotion after restart. Host restart runs MissionManager.recover(), which ends every STAGED record: manager.server.ts:4625-4626 loops over staging.inState("STAGED") and calls endStaged(..., "INVALIDATED_BY_HOST_RESTART"). endStaged (manager.server.ts:2581-2595) also denies the linked request (resolvedAt set, resolution "deny"). promoteStaged then refuses any non-STAGED record (manager.server.ts:2639-2641), so the pre-crash change cannot be promoted after restart. The only route left is a new staging after restart while a pre-crash orphan survives. That variant is not what the finding describes, and it still depends on the orphan surviving at all.

3. Survival itself is unverified. Provider children are plain spawn without the native KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE job (adapters.server.ts:208 via trackOwnedChild, which only adds to an in-memory Set). Windows does not kill children on parent death, so survival is plausible. A provider writing to a broken stdout pipe may exit, though, and nothing in the code path proves otherwise. The finding itself says it is not runtime-verified.

4. Authority impact is low. The orphan is code the workstation already authorized under a write Mission. Promotion requires the Windows owner to approve the exact reviewed bytes (promoteStaged re-checks hash and destination). The phone gains no execution authority, which the finding concedes.

Probes were not run because the refutation rests on code reading and the documented-residual status. Had it been real and not documented, the honest severity would be LOW, not MEDIUM: defense-in-depth loss, owner-reviewed bytes, workstation-authorized surviving code, and a repro that needs a post-restart staging to demonstrate.

Refuted on three independent grounds, all from code reading in the working tree (no runtime probe was run).

1. The repro's promotion step cannot succeed after a Host restart. On restart, every record still in STAGED is invalidated: src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:4625-4626 calls endStaged(record, "INVALIDATED_BY_HOST_RESTART") for each STAGED record ("a Retry stages the change again for a fresh review"). promoteStaged then refuses any record whose promotionState is not STAGED (manager.server.ts:2639-2641). The only remaining route is a restart-reconciled record, and that is never re-promoted by the gate. So repro step 5 ("approve promotion of the staged change") is refused, and the claimed bypass does not occur for the change staged before the crash.

2. The residual is documented. MA3_T9R_F01_SECURITY_CLOSURE.md section 7 item 5 states: "Survivor tracking is in memory. Processes surviving a Host restart are not tracked; remote envelopes are revoked at restart." MA3_T9R_F02_AUTHORIZATION_EDGE_CLOSURE.md section 4 item 4 (survivor-lineage MEDIUM, F01 section 7.4 residual) and item 6 ("survivor tracking is in memory") cover the same behavior. The finding's mechanism (in-memory lingering/lingeringAttempt/owned set, no reseed, watchSurvivors only at manager.server.ts:1431 and :1654) is exactly what is documented, and the restart-specific framing does not add a new authority path.

3. Any path that reaches promotion with the survivor alive requires a fresh device-proposed change staged after restart. That needs a new remote envelope, since remote envelopes are revoked at restart (manager.server.ts:4627 onward). The phone still gains no execution authority; the owner performs the promotion; the survivor already holds workstation-approved shell authority, so the gate's only effect is timing of a read, which is the accepted "arbitrary programs can read promoted files" residual.

Severity if it were real: MEDIUM at most, as the finding itself says. It is not demonstrably real in the stated repro, and it is a documented residual, so it should not be re-reported.
